observedProblem: V2-D Host Implementation was dispatched before the orchestrator generated an immediate pre-edit structural baseline. The producer discovered the omission after editing, and the older Batch F snapshot cannot establish an unbroken provenance chain for the current target files.
whyExistingGatePassed: The structural diff validator checked baseline versus current content but did not prove who captured the baseline or when.
The apply-host sequence assigned baseline creation to the Host Implementation role during diagnosis, allowing the producer to control its own evidence.
The receipt gate ran after edits and had no dispatch-time source hash check.
evidencePolicy: Do not manufacture or backdate a current baseline. Batch F may remain historical evidence, but cannot be chained into V2-D unless its recorded source SHA is independently proven identical to the exact pre-edit V2-D target.
correctiveAction: Added orchestrator-only prepare-bundle with route, source file, source SHA-256, baseline file, baseline SHA-256 and timestamp.
Added dispatch verification that blocks when a target changed after capture.
Added receipt verification that baseline artifacts and source identity still match the frozen bundle.
Moved baseline ownership out of Host Implementation in the workflow sequence.
Explicitly prohibited producer-authored or post-edit refreshed baselines.
candidateValidation: Promote after a fresh apply-host run proves that dispatch is blocked both for edited-before-dispatch sources and producer-owned bundles, then receipt succeeds using the original frozen artifacts.
nonActions: No host production file was changed.
No baseline was fabricated for V2-D.
No previous QA verdict was changed.
